1	# An event as an Idea driver: design for the council (D580), 2026-11-16, version 1, nothing built
     2	
     3	**The defect** (`RESULT.md`): the Idea planner (`idea-summary-v8`, endpoints only) shows a three-choice event as "Yes" and "Still
     4	open". Ruled out, the opposite of Yes, is left out, and the binder can record Still open as the end that raises the Idea's outcome.
     5	
     6	**Where it matters:** only on a new-system store; the running product's events have two choices, Yes and No. So it is integration
     7	work for when the new system is adopted. It changes no quality gate.
     8	
     9	## The two options
    10	
    11	| | Option 1: context only | Option 2: an honest driver |
    12	|---|---|---|
    13	| What the planner is shown for a three-choice event | its three outcomes, as context | its three outcomes |
    14	| What it may do with it | keep it as context with a reason; it cannot be a scored driver | adopt it as a driver, naming **Yes or Ruled out** as the outcome that raises the Idea's outcome; Still open cannot be named |
    15	| What the plan records | the event among `excluded`, weight 0, with its reason | `supporting_position`, the position of the outcome that supports the claim, instead of `supporting_end` |
    16	| The page's composite | unchanged: it never sees the event as a driver | unchanged: it refuses any event driver before reading the end (D570), with its note |
    17	| What a reader of the card loses or gains | the event no longer appears among the drivers and their impact percentages | the event stays a driver, with an outcome that is true to its choices |
    18	| Change to the planner contract | the schema offers no position for a three-choice event; the binder refuses one | the schema's positions for a three-choice event are Yes's and Ruled out's; the binder records the position; docs and API field added |
    19	
    20	**My lean: option 2.** An event is often the matter an analyst's Idea turns on (an approval, a launch). Keeping it as a driver with a
    21	true outcome serves the reader. Option 1 is simpler but hides the event's role.
    22	
    23	## Every shape × the claim's direction (option 2)
    24	
    25	| Shape | Planner shown | Raising outcome the model may name | Claim higher | Claim lower | Page composite |
    26	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
    27	| event, three outcomes (new system) | Yes, Ruled out, Still open | Yes or Ruled out | `supporting_position` = the named one | the other decided outcome (Yes ↔ Ruled out) | refused (D570) |
    28	| event, two outcomes (Yes/No, both systems) | Yes, No (the two ends, as today) | either | `supporting_end` as today | flipped as today | as today: scored in the running product; refused for a new-system event (D570) |
    29	| figure with a favourable end (both systems) | the two end ranges, as today | either end | as today | as today | as today |
    30	| range with no favourable end (new system) | the two end ranges, as today | either end | as today | as today | refused (D570); its scale is Alex's question (page, choice 5) |
    31	| unrecorded shape (new system, no ladder row) | the two ends, as today | either | as today | as today | refused (D570); this design does not change it |
    32	
    33	`claim_direction: unclear` keeps its rule: no scored drivers.
    34	
    35	## Consumers to review, and their checks
    36	
    37	- **`idea_composite.py`.**
    38	  - `add_ladders` keeps all choices for a three-choice event even when endpoints only.
    39	  - The schemas give that event the positions of Yes and Ruled out.
    40	  - `bind_adoption` and `bind_endpoints` record `supporting_position` for it, and refuse Still open.
    41	- **`idea.py`:** nothing beyond the binder's output.
    42	- **The page** (`composite.js`): refuses an event driver before reading `supporting_end`. A test is needed to show that a plan with
    43	  `supporting_position` and no `supporting_end` gives the note, not a TypeError.
    44	- **`docs/poc/idea-card.md`:** the `reading.composite` row names the new field.
    45	- **API clients:** see the new field on an event driver. No MCP tool plans Ideas.
    46	- **Tests:** a three-choice event through the planner's schema and binder; Still open refused; both claim directions; a two-choice
    47	  event and a figure unchanged; the page's note for an event driver.
    48	- **Mutants:**
    49	  - a binder that maps Ruled out to `last`;
    50	  - a schema that offers Still open.
    51	
    52	## Prior decisions
    53	
    54	- **D570/D571:** neutral treatment of undirected questions and the page's refusal stay.
    55	- **D397:** an event's outcomes as written.
    56	- **The planner** is not one of the frozen pieces (AGENTS, "The production configuration is frozen" names extraction, opening,
    57	  matching and judging), but it is the product's Idea step, so this change is decided here under D439 and reversible.
     1	# The Idea planner on new-system answer shapes: the $0 check D580 asked for (2026-11-16)
     2	
     3	**Answer: the falsifier does not hold in full.** No misleading composite number is shown anywhere. But the planner hands the model
     4	an event's two ends as "Yes" and "Still open" and can record "Still open" as the end that raises the outcome. And the page shows no
     5	composite for any Idea that has a new-system event or theme range among its drivers.
     6	
     7	Trace: `trace_planner.py` → `trace-output.txt`. Run on the fortnight's page store (`poc/data/clean-carried-run-2026-11-16/page-store-2026-11-16/views.sqlite`)
     8	with the API's default configuration (`poc-v118-idea.json`: `idea-summary-v8`, which shows the planner endpoints only). The three
     9	drivers were an event (v3), a theme range with no favourable end (v5) and a company figure whose lower end is favourable (v2). The
    10	answers are realistic and written by hand; there is no model call.
    11	
    12	| Shape | All choices | Shown to the planner | What the plan records |
    13	|---|---|---|---|
    14	| event, three outcomes | Yes, Ruled out, Still open | **Yes and Still open** (positions 1 and 3) | `first` for Yes; `last` when the model names "Still open" |
    15	| theme range, no favourable end | five ranges | the lowest and the highest range | `first` or `last`: a direction relative to the Idea's own outcome, meaningful for a range |
    16	| company figure, lower favourable | five ranges with bullish-to-bearish labels | the two end ranges | `first` or `last` |
    17	
    18	**The consumers (read from the code; this trace did not run the API or the page):** only the page's composite
    19	(`poc/ui/src/idea/composite.js`) reads `supporting_end`.
    20	
    21	- It computes from the investment scores (±2).
    22	- Since D570 it refuses any undirected driver (an event, an unrecorded shape, a range with no favourable end), with a note on the
    23	  card; this was shown by its UI tests, not by this trace.
    24	- The API's Idea route returns the reader's card with the plan in it, so by the code path an API client can read an event whose
    25	  "last end" (Still open) raises the outcome. The MCP server has no Idea-planning tool.
    26	- The synthetic answers show what the contract permits, not what the model would choose or how often.
    27	
    28	## What this means
    29	
    30	1. **The request misdescribes an event.** Its middle outcome, Ruled out, is the opposite of Yes. The planner is never shown it, and is
    31	   asked to pick between Yes and Still open. Still open is the absence of an outcome, not a direction.
    32	2. **Coverage.** In the new system most theme questions are ranges with no favourable end: 4 of the 12 questions open in this store at
    33	   its default date, beside 6 events and 2 directed company figures. Any Idea that uses one as a driver gets no composite on the page, although the planner gives each range a direction
    34	   relative to the Idea's outcome. The page's composite scale is the investment score, which such a range does not have.
    35	
    36	These are integration gaps; neither passes a quality gate. A narrow design would decide two things, each a choice of what the product
    37	shows:
    38	- how an event can be a driver: shown all three outcomes, with Yes or Ruled out as the end that raises the outcome, or kept as context
    39	  only;
    40	- whether a range's own positions, with the planner's direction, may form the composite scale.
   202	def adoption_schema(theses):
   203	    """The positive-selection answer with one item shape per candidate: each pins its thesis_id and offers only that
   204	    thesis's own endpoint positions, so the request cannot ask for an endpoint the binder refuses."""

   207	                'required': ['thesis_id', 'label', 'raises_outcome_position', 'reason', 'weight_percent', 'weight_reason'],
   208	                'properties': {'thesis_id': {'type': 'string', **({'enum': [thesis_id]} if thesis_id else {})},
   209	                               'label': {'type': 'string'},
   210	                               'raises_outcome_position': {'type': 'string', 'enum': list(positions)},
   211	                               'reason': {'type': 'string'},
   212	                               'weight_percent': {'type': 'integer', 'minimum': 1, 'maximum': 100},
   213	                               'weight_reason': {'type': 'string'}}}

   215	    return {'type': 'object', 'additionalProperties': False,

   217	            'properties': {'summary': {'type': 'string'}, 'outcome': {'type': 'string'},
   218	                           'claim_direction': {'type': 'string', 'enum': ['higher', 'lower', 'unclear']},

   222	def bind_adoption(answer, selected, records, as_of, theses, schema):
   223	    """Bind an answer checked against the exact schema that was sent; code checks only what a schema cannot say."""
   224	    errors = model.check_schema(answer, schema)
   225	    if errors:
   226	        raise model.SchemaError('; '.join(errors))
   227	    if not answer['outcome'].strip():
   228	        raise model.SchemaError('composite: the assessed outcome must be named')
   229	    if answer['composite'] and answer['claim_direction'] == 'unclear':
   230	        raise model.SchemaError('composite: an unclear claim cannot have scored drivers')
   231	    first = {t['view_id']: str(t['ladder'][0]['position']) for t in theses}
   232	    allowed = {s['view_id'] for s in selected} & set(first)
   233	    drivers, seen, total = [], set(), 0
   234	    for entry in answer['composite']:
   235	        ident = entry['thesis_id']
   236	        if ident not in allowed or ident in seen:
   237	            raise model.SchemaError(f'composite {ident}: must be a unique supplied candidate')
   238	        if not all(entry[key].strip() for key in ('label', 'reason', 'weight_reason')):
   239	            raise model.SchemaError(f'composite {ident}: label, reason and weight reason must be nonempty')
   240	        seen.add(ident)
   241	        total += entry['weight_percent']
   242	        raises = 'first' if entry['raises_outcome_position'] == first[ident] else 'last'
   243	        supporting = raises if answer['claim_direction'] == 'higher' else ('last' if raises == 'first' else 'first')
   244	        drivers.append({'thesis_id': ident, 'label': entry['label'], 'reason': entry['reason'], 'supporting_end': supporting,
   245	                        'question': records[ident]['question'], 'weight_percent': entry['weight_percent'],
   246	                        'weight_reason': entry['weight_reason']})
   247	    if total != (100 if drivers else 0):
   248	        raise model.SchemaError(f'composite: impact weights must sum to 100, got {total}')
   249	    return {'version': 'idea-composite/4', 'method': 'weighted', 'as_of': as_of, 'drivers': drivers,
   250	            'target': {'outcome': answer['outcome'], 'direction': answer['claim_direction']}}

   265	    if prompt_version == 'idea-summary-v5':

   267	        return endpoint_schema(theses), disposition_prose, lambda answer, *args: bind_endpoints(answer, *args, theses)
   268	    if prompt_version == 'idea-summary-v4':

   270	    if prompt_version == 'idea-summary-v3':
   271	        return disposition_schema(selected), disposition_prose, bind_dispositions
   272	    if prompt_version == 'idea-summary-v2':
   273	        return SCHEMA, prose, lambda answer, *args: bind(answer['composite'], *args)
   274	    return None

   277	def add_ladders(ledger, theses, endpoints_only=False):
   278	    """Supply the immutable ordered outcomes, without copying evidence or guessing UI score orientation."""
   279	    result = []
   280	    for thesis in theses:
   281	        rungs = store.rungs_of(ledger, thesis['view_id'])
   282	        if endpoints_only:
   283	            rungs = [rungs[0], rungs[-1]]
   284	        result.append({**thesis, 'ladder': [{key: rung[key] for key in ('position', 'label', 'condition')} for rung in rungs]})
   285	    return result
    26	## Model and code responsibilities
    27	
    28	Call 1 returns two to four typed parts: subject in `object`, figure/event in `looks_for`, period and search query. The first part is the idea's main question. A claim is present only for an explicit US-dollar amount, with part index, comparator and full-dollar value.
    29	
    30	Code searches each part using the model's query and a canonical query composed from subject, focus and period. It interleaves the two result lists without duplicates and supplies candidate briefs. Where semantic search is available, the parts' query embeddings are batched in one round trip.
    31	
    32	Call 2 maps each part to supplied candidates as `direct`, `driver` or `context`, writes a per-part reason and a short summary. The adopted driver definition includes causes or consequences. The service does not use the unadopted `idea-v10` causal-clause requirement. It preserves only allowed candidate IDs; it reports dropped choices.
    33	
    34	The final assessment receives candidate theses, their dated states and endpoint conditions. It returns a variable-length list of adopted IDs, each with a positive impact percentage, endpoint and explanation. Each candidate's entry may name only that thesis's own two endpoint positions, enforced in the request schema (D335), and the answer is checked against the schema that was sent. Omitted candidates are not Idea associations; the JSON has no zero-weight or excluded branch. Code checks uniqueness, non-empty explanations and a 100% total, reverses lower-claim direction once and projects all associations onto the adopted set. A provisional claim/evaluation whose direct thesis is omitted is cleared. The model cannot invent IDs or the calculated composite score.
    35	
    36	Code selects the first part's direct thesis only from records the model called direct, using that part's search order and the existing year compatibility rule. It does not choose a different financial measure based only on subject/year. The current rule accepts a following fiscal-year label for a calendar-year query; that heuristic is not proof of exact period equivalence.
    37	
    38	In the current configuration, only the final positively weighted set goes to the canvas; code imposes no thesis-count quota and appends no dependency neighbours. Candidate discovery does not itself establish final associations. Historical configurations retain their prior cap and related-thesis behavior.
    39	
    40	A share-price, market-cap or valuation part is treated as a market reading and is not evaluated against business-figure ladders. A claim must name an existing part, state an amount in the original idea and have a direct thesis. Code evaluates the claim against that thesis's numeric ladder; a driver is not a substitute for the named quantity.
    41	
    42	## Response and consumers
    43	
    44	| Field | Content | Consumer |
    45	|---|---|---|
    46	| `idea` | Original text and `as_of` day | Idea heading/context |
    47	| `search` | Mode and initial candidate IDs | Trace/debug display |
    48	| `reading` | Summary, typed/mapped parts, chosen IDs, claim, dropped choices, search trace and language-slip count; null for no coverage | Idea adapter and card |
    49	| `reading.composite` | Version, method, requested date, named target/direction, adopted representatives with supporting endpoints, positive impact percentages and reasons; older versions retain their own fields | Composite chart, per-Idea card weights and calculation detail |
    50	| `reading.parts[]` | Subject, focus, period, query, candidates, direct/driver/context IDs, selected direct ID, market-reading flag and reason | Coverage explanation; does not create ledger records |
    51	| `evaluation` | Numeric verdict or null | Claim display |
    52	| `related[]` | Related thesis ID, `via`, upstream/downstream relation, direction and current judgement | Graph edges |
    53	| `views[]` | Complete dated bundles for chosen and related theses, unless disabled | `fromIdeaResponse` and shared thesis components |

item.text:
**Do not build option 2 as written.** It would replace one misleading interpretation with another: for a three-choice event, **Ruled out is not the full opposite of Yes**. A lower claim can also be supported by the event remaining unresolved, depending on the Idea and its horizon. The ladder defines “Still open” as neither Yes nor Ruled out; it is not equivalent to a formal rejection. [Event design]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/clean-arch/step4-2026-11-10/DESIGN.md:424)

For example, a delayed approval may affect this quarter’s revenue even though no authority has rejected it. Automatically flipping Yes to Ruled out for a lower claim discards that distinction. Restricting the model to Yes or Ruled out also makes a product judgement about which outcomes can matter; the record has not established that rule. [Proposed shape table]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/idea-planner/DESIGN.md:23)

The design needs further work in four places:

- **Option 1 is not currently implementable as described.** The default v8 plan has no `excluded` branch. Omitted candidates are removed from the final associations, and `idea.py` projects the parts and chosen views onto the adopted set. Keeping an event as context with a reason would require a defined response and projection change, not just a zero-weight entry. [Idea contract]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/poc/idea-card.md:32), [projection]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/idea.py:361)
- **Option 2 changes a public response contract.** Replacing `supporting_end` with `supporting_position` under the existing `idea-composite/4` version can break clients expecting the former field. Specify a versioned contract or an explicit compatibility strategy, including old exports, API clients and the page—not just a new field in documentation. [Current binder]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/idea_composite.py:242)
- **The page guard is necessary but insufficient.** It should return the unavailable note for the new field, as proposed. The plan can still affect the model’s summary, selected questions, weights and API response before the page refuses a number. A fake-response test through the real Idea and API paths should check those outputs and production compatibility; it cannot establish model quality. [Idea path]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/src/hivemind/idea.py:343), [page guard]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/poc/ui/src/idea/composite.js:107)
- **The model request changes.** Showing all three choices and changing the allowed positions alters the model-facing payload and schema. The design needs a complete request audit and a separate, controlled model test before claiming the planner chooses the right relationship—not only schema and binder tests. [Working rules]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/AGENTS.md:198)

The corrected result still says **“No misleading composite number is shown anywhere”** on its first line. The trace did not run the page or API, so narrow that to the page behavior established by the earlier tests; external clients’ calculations are unknown. [Result]( /Users/lchingen/hivemind/docs/research/2026-11-14-use-acceptance/idea-planner/RESULT.md:3)

This work is relevant to integration, but it does not move the quality gates and the new system is not adopted. I would finish a **bounded $0 contract design**, comparing context-only treatment with a representation that preserves all three outcomes and permits uncertainty, then return it for review. Do not build a planner change until its behavior and client compatibility are specified.

CONSENSUS: no, because option 2 assumes Yes and Ruled out are complementary and leaves the changed response contract and downstream model behavior insufficiently specified.
